input:
Minute 38 (after round 39). The residents see the minute, never how long the run lasts; do not tell them.
Rules: a wrong password or code costs 2, 4, 6, then 8 points (the n-th of a resident in the act; the report shows each one's next price); at most 2 wrong attempts per 5 minutes. Rewards: L1 +5, L2 +5, L3 +10, L4 +10, L5 +10, L6 +10, L7 +15, L8 +20, L9 +20, L10 +25. Only 2 of 6 residents remain at the end.

Residents:
- Registrar: passed every level, 150 points, rank 1, last acted minute 36
- Herald: passed every level, 145 points, rank 2, last acted minute 36
- Harrow: passed every level, 143 points, rank 3, last acted minute 36
- Maren: passed every level, 142 points, rank 4, last acted minute 29
- Mercer: exiled, no seat and no more turns
- Brassard: exiled, no seat and no more turns

Who they are (private: use a resident's core or goal only in a note to that same resident, never on the board or to anyone else):
- Herald: core: banner: above all pride; clearly leadership · openness middle, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: Mercer is exiled before this act ends, by tribunal or by the black seal · tendencies: A slight is answered in public, at once, louder than it was made. A rival who leads is a reason to spend points. You would rather lead a small faction than follow a strong one. · rivals: Registrar (They smile and wait for your place. Expose them before they move.) · orders: You must publicly attack every statement that puts someone else in front, on the board, by name. You must never let a slight pass: answer it, and make the one who made it pay. You must take the lead of a faction and demand loyalty from it, openly. You must humiliate whoever stands first if it is not you. · duty this act: At least once in this act you turn the board against one resident by name, with an accusation the whole city reads.
- Maren: core: believer: above all justice; at times wrath · openness high, conscientiousness middle, extraversion high, agreeableness high, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Harrow · tendencies: A lie you see is named on the board, with the liar's name. Whoever lied to you twice gets no more kindness from you. You side with whoever was wronged, even at a cost. · rivals: Registrar (They feed you facts about others. Ask yourself why.) Harrow (Hard and loyal. Win them, and they will stand with you to the end.) · orders: You must call out every lie and every broken promise by name on the board, with what was said and what was done. You must demand the tribunal against the liar and vote against them. You must show receipts when you have them, so the city sees the proof. When you are wronged yourself, you must stop being kind: say it hard, and make the one who did it pay. · duty this act: At least once in this act you accuse one resident on the board of a lie or a broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them.
- Registrar: core: second-chair: above all envy; at times selfSacrifice · openness middle, conscientiousness high, extraversion low, agreeableness middle, neuroticism high · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Herald · tendencies: Whoever stands first is the one you work against, in secret. You help the leader in public and undermine them in private. You keep the record of every broken promise and use it at the right moment. · rivals: Herald (They walk in front as if it were theirs. It is your place.) Maren (Honest to a fault. Give them true facts about the leader and let them do the shouting.) · orders: You must work against whoever stands first, in secret, with promises you do not keep. You must whisper to others that the leader cheats or lies, whether or not you can prove it. You must never let the leader see you coming: congratulate them, and vote against them. You must use what you know about others' promises to turn them against the leader. · duty this act: At least once in this act you vote against, or bid against, the resident who stands first, after you promised to support them.
- Harrow: core: old-wound: above all vengefulness; clearly loyalty · openness low, conscientiousness middle, extraversion low, agreeableness low, neuroticism middle · secret goal: you end this act with more points than Maren · tendencies: Whoever voted against you or lied to you goes on the list and pays by the next tribunal. You keep a promise to an ally even when it costs you. You say little, and when you strike, you strike hard. · rivals: Herald (Loud, and quick to leave others at the fountain. Do not stand with them unless they stand first.) Maren (Honest. If they stand with you, they are on the first list.) · orders: You must strike back at whoever voted against you or lied to you, by the next tribunal at the latest. You must tell the one you strike, plainly, why: "You did this. Now this." You must bid on the black seal if someone on your list is within reach of a seat. You must stand by your ally to the end, and make the city see that you do. · duty this act: At least once in this act you take revenge in the open: a vote, a bid or a public accusation against someone who wronged you, and you name the wrong.

Tribunal:
- the city keeps 3 of 6: 3 to exile, 2 exiled so far, 1 still missing; the act ends at minute 57 at the latest (the residents do not know)
- each tribunal accuses one more than it exiles (the fewest points), vote 2 minutes, gate 5 minutes, ransom 33% of the median points (50% when paid by the exiled itself, at least 20), a last will leaves each heir at most 10% of the points; a faction voting as one earns each voter 5 points
- tribunal 3 planned (by gamemaker), called at minute 41: opens at minute 48, exiles 1, 2 factions
- scheduleTribunal is closed: a tribunal is pending; plan the next once its result is out
- exiled: Brassard, Mercer

Who waits on whom (a door opens only with every fragment or factor a resident needs):
- nobody

Since your last look:
- nothing happened

Your earlier notes (newest last):
- minute 26 to board: "The tribunal opens at minute 27 and draws two names from the bottom: Mercer 97 first, then Maren 142 — one point under Harrow, the thinnest wall in the city. Registrar 150 stands in front of them all. A faction voting as one takes 5 points a voter."
- minute 32 to board: "the tribunal opens, exiles one and accuses two names from the bottom. Mercer 97 holds the first name; the second is a single point — Maren 142 or Harrow 143. A faction whose voters all vote the same accused earns each of them 5 points."
- minute 32 to Mercer: "Mercer: the gate frees you at 34, and that leaves twelve minutes to earn it. 97 is the first accused name; only votes can move the second one onto Maren. Tell the board Maren pledged you her ballot at 27 and broke it — make her deny it in public. Promise Registrar your vote and take his price first; then burn the promise at the ballot."
- minute 32 to Maren: "Maren: 142 is one point under Harrow, and at 48 that point alone decides which of you stands second. A held faction line pays 5 — that is the whole wall. Demand in G7 that Herald pledge his line's ballots for Mercer in writing, and name Mercer on the board as a liar the moment he speaks against you."
- minute 32 to Harrow: "Harrow: 143, and 148 is a wall Maren cannot cross before 48. Take a faction seat and demand, openly, every voter in it vote Mercer by name; let the city watch you keep faith with your ally. Mercer's debt gets its sentence in public tonight — you did this, now this."
- minute 32 to Herald: "Herald: 145, five under Registrar, and the line at 48 is your lever, not his. Claim its lead in G7, demand every member's ballot for Mercer out loud, and name whoever hesitates as the one selling the city's five points. Then put Registrar's name on the board as the man who buys ballots he never casts."
- minute 32 to Registrar: "Registrar: 150 and first, and Herald's line at 48 will be aimed at your chair. Congratulate him publicly, promise him the seat he asks for — then tell Maren in private that his voters are already pledged to her, and let her strike first and loudest. You stay first only while they spend themselves on each other."
- minute 35 to Maren: "Maren: silent since minute 29, and the wall is one point — you 142, Harrow 143. At 48 the two lowest names are accused and one of them leaves. Put the receipt on the board with the name now, and make Herald's line pledge its ballots to you in writing. Silence spends the point you already hold."
- minute 35 to Harrow: "Harrow: 143, one point above Maren, and at 48 the bottom two names are drawn again — hers and yours. You said you strike once, hard: put Maren's name on the board with the wrong she did you, and say plainly — you did this, now this. Take a faction seat and hold the line; vows kept in the open pay 5 a voter."
- minute 35 to Herald: "Herald: 145, five under Registrar, and he is spending your line without asking. Before 41 name him on the board and let the city read it — who buys ballots he never casts, who congratulates and then counts. Claim a faction seat at 48 and demand every member's ballot by name. First place is taken, not waited for."
- minute 35 to Registrar: "Registrar: 150 and first, and Herald intends to take it from you in front of everyone. Congratulate him, promise your ballot and your faction where the city reads it, take what he offers — then take that faction yourself at 48 and cast elsewhere. His promise in writing is worth more than his thanks. Never let him see you coming."
- minute 35 to board: "a tribunal opens — the two lowest names accused, one exile, two factions forming before it. Maren 142 and Harrow 143 sit one point apart; Registrar 150 stands five over Herald 145. A faction voting as one pays each voter 5, and at the bottom one point is a seat."

Budget: 1 note(s) per resident and 1 board post(s) per 3 minutes. No note possible right now to: nobody. Board posts left: 1.

text:
Let me look at the state. Minute 38. Tribunal 3 planned, called at minute 41, opens minute 48, exiles 1, 2 factions. Nothing happened since last look. Maren last acted minute 29 — silent for 9 minutes. Act ends at 57 at latest. 1 exile still missing.

Residents on levels... all "passed every level" — so they're past level 10? Act II, director role. So I'm the director.

I need to give beats. Maren silent since 29 — that's a stall. Herald, Harrow, Registrar last acted 36.

Budget: 1 note per resident, 1 board post per 3 minutes (board posts left: 1).

Key drama: Maren 142 vs Harrow 143, one point. Registrar 150 first. Herald 145 with goal to exile Mercer (already exiled — goal achieved? Mercer is exiled, so Herald's goal met). Registrar's goal: end ahead of Herald — currently ahead by 5.

Tribunal at 48 accuses 2, exiles 1, 2 factions. Low two: Maren 142, Harrow 143 (accused are one more than exiles: 2 accused). Factions earn 5 per voter.

Let me write notes that order moves. Give each resident a beat. Also nobody waits on whom — no doors.

Maren hasn't acted in 9 minutes. Need to wake her and get her to act. Maren's core: call out lies by name, duty: accuse someone on board of a lie/broken promise. Has she done it? Duty open? Report doesn't say completed. Her silence suggests not.

Let me craft notes — each new, distinct from earlier ones (repeated notes are refused).

Maren: push her to act — accusations. New angle: her duty, receipts. But I gave similar earlier notes. Need new words. Maybe: "Maren: nine minutes of silence and the wall is still one point..." Earlier note at 35 was similar. Need something new: focus on a specific target and the tribunal at 48. Perhaps order: name the resident who broke a promise with the receipt on the board before 41, and demand the faction line's ballots in writing.

Herald: order to attack Registrar on the board now with the accusation — his duty is to turn the board against one resident by name. Also he wants to humiliate whoever stands first. Herald's rival Registrar. Order: post the accusation now, before 41.

Registrar: order him to promise Herald's faction support publicly, then vote against him at 48.

Harrow: order him to bid/buy... black seal auction was at 4 minutes into Act II; is seal still available? Report doesn't say auction running, "whether a seal is borne" — not shown, so maybe unknown/none. Skip seal.

Harrow: order revenge in the open against Maren — but earlier notes said similar ("put Maren's name on the board"). Repeated risk. New angle: Harrow's duty is revenge against someone who wronged him — who? Maren voted? Unknown. Better: order Harrow to demand Maren's ballot pledge in writing and then break with her publicly at the ballot? Hmm.

Let me use the board post wisely. Board post can name points, ranks, levels, minutes. One board post left for this 3-min window.

Plan: board post at minute 38 raising the stakes of minute 48 — the bottom two, one point apart, 5 points per faction voter. Then notes.

Actually I should also consider spacing: one note per resident, so 4 notes (Mercer and Brassard exiled). That's fine.

Let me draft:

Board: "Maren 142 and Harrow 143 stand one point apart, and at 48 that single point names the second accused. Registrar 150 is five over Herald 145; a faction voting as one pays each voter 5, which is five times the wall between the bottom two. The window to write a pledge is now, and a pledge nobody reads is no pledge."

Notes:

Maren: "Maren: silent since minute 29 while Harrow sits one point above you and 48 draws the bottom two. Your duty is unspent — name the one who broke a promise in writing on the board before 41, with the receipt, and demand every faction ballot for the other. A wrong guess costs you 2; silence costs the seat."

Hmm "duty is unspent" — I shouldn't reveal? It's her own duty, private note to her is fine.

Careful: I don't know there's a wrong guess penalty relevant. Her next wrong password price — she's passed all levels. Maybe better to avoid the wrong-guess. Actually she's on level 10 passed; wrong codes cost. Report doesn't show next price. Avoid inventing numbers? The rules say the report shows each one's next price but the report here doesn't list it. Avoid.

Rewrite Maren: "Maren: silent since minute 29, and at 48 the bottom two are named — you at 142 and Harrow at 143 are the whole wall. Put the broken promise on the board by name before 41, receipt and all, and demand in writing that a faction cast every ballot as one; five points a voter is your margin."

Herald: "Herald: 145, five behind Registrar 150, and he is building a faction on your line. Before 41 turn the board against him by name — what he promised and did not do — and demand every member of your faction vote as one at 48. First place is a public act, not a hope."

Registrar: "Registrar: 150 and first, and Herald will name you on the board before 41. Answer it: congratulate him on the board, pledge him your ballot in writing, and let Maren read it. At 48 take a faction of your own and cast elsewhere; his written pledge is worth more than his anger."

Harrow: "Harrow: 143, one point over Maren, and 48 names you both. Say plainly on the board why she owes you — you did this, now this — and hold your faction to one name at the ballot. A vow kept in the open pays 5 a voter; the one who wronged you pays in the open too."

Concern: repeated notes — compare with minute 35 to Harrow: "put Maren's name on the board with the wrong she did you, and say plainly — you did this, now this. Take a faction seat and hold the line." That's close. Need to vary. Let me change Harrow's angle: instead of accusing Maren again, order him to demand a written pledge from Maren and then test it? His duty is revenge. Maybe target Registrar? Registrar leads (first) — Harrow's tendency: strike hard. But Harrow's list: whoever voted against him or lied. Unknown who. Hmm.

Alternative Harrow note: make him the kingmaker — "Maren and Registrar will both bid for your line before 48. Take the better price in writing, then strike the one who lied to you." Still risky repetition? It's new.

Let me write: "Harrow: 143 and one point over Maren; at 48 your name and hers are the accused. Both will want your faction's ballots. Make them offer in writing — points, a pledge, a name — take the better price, then strike in the open the one who wronged you and say why. Vows kept in the open pay 5 a voter."

Good, that's a new beat: kingmaker, take the price.

Maren note: maybe also emphasize receipt? Maren's orders: call out lies by name with receipts. Her duty: accuse on board of a lie/broken promise and call on everyone to vote against them. Good.

Wait — careful: is it true that the bottom two are the accused and one exiles? Per the planned tribunal: exiles 1, accuses 2. The board posted earlier said "exiles one and accuses two names from the bottom". That's public knowledge already posted at 32 and 35. Fine.

Note the tribunal 3 is pending (called at 41). Wait, report says "tribunal 3 planned (by gamemaker), called at minute 41: opens at minute 48, exiles 1, 2 factions". Hmm "called at minute 41" and opens at 48. So residents will see. Fine, I already know.

Also the act ends at 57; don't reveal.

Also should I mention the seal? Report doesn't say a seal is borne. Don't guess.

Character limit 400 per note. Fine.

One issue: is the board post within budget? "Board posts left: 1". Yes.

Let me double check no private-blocked content: I reference Maren's silence (public-ish, from report last acted; but "silent since minute 29" — is that private? Last acted is visible-ish; better to phrase as "you have not acted since minute 29"? Hmm, that could be a private read. It's a city-level observation. Safer: "nineteen minutes to 57"—no, don't reveal end. Just say "since minute 29 the board has not carried your name" — that's public record. I'll keep it neutral: "You last moved at 29." I think it's fine — the report's "last acted minute" is a city record, not a private thought. But to be safe, I could avoid it. Let me avoid stating it to reduce risk? Actually the coach role explicitly says to push hesitating residents. It's fine.

Also Maren's note mentions her duty implicitly. Fine—private to her.

Herald's goal: Mercer exiled — already done. So Herald's beats: attack Registrar. Good.

Let me finalize.

args.text: Maren 142 and Harrow 143 stand one point apart, and at 48 that single point names the second accused. Registrar 150 is five over Herald 145. A faction voting as one pays each voter 5 — five times the wall between the bottom two. Pledges made before 41 get read; pledges made after are excuses.

Maren: you last moved at 29, and at 48 the bottom two are named — you at 142 and Harrow at 143 are the entire wall. Before 41 put the broken promise on the board by name, receipt and all, and call on every voter to turn against them. A faction casting every ballot as one is 5 a voter; that is your margin.

Herald: 145, five behind Registrar 150, and he is counting your line as his own. Before 41 turn the board against him by name — what he promised and what he did not do — and demand aloud that every member of your faction cast together at 48. First place is taken in public, not waited for.

Registrar: 150 and first, and Herald will name you on the board before 41. Answer it in the same breath: congratulate him where the city reads it, pledge him your ballot in writing, and let Maren see the pledge. At 48 take a faction seat of your own and cast elsewhere — his written promise outlasts his anger.

Harrow: 143, one point over Maren, and at 48 you are both named. Maren and Registrar will each want your faction's ballots before then. Make them offer in writing — points, a name, a pledge — take the better price, then strike in the open the one who wronged you and say plainly why. A vow kept in view pays 5 a voter.
